title: Germany news: Far-right AfD gets first house speaker in a German state parliament
summary: An AfD member has become speaker in Saxony-Anhalt's state parliament with the help of the populist BSW party. And Germany's foreign minister has warned that the climate crisis could fuel extremism.…

image.caption: Tobias Rausch has been elected as speaker in Saxony-Anhalt's parliamentImage: Jan Woitas/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Far-right AfD candidate elected state parliamentary speaker

blocks.caption: Tobias Rausch has been in the Saxony-Anhalt parliament since 2016Image: dts-Agentur/picture alliance

blocks.text: Tobias Rausch, the far-right Alternative for Germany's (AFD's) nomination for speaker in Saxony-Anhalt's state parliament, has been elected with the help of the populist BSW party.
Rausch gained 48 votes from 82 eligible votes. There were five abstentions.

The AfD holds 39 seats in the parliament and the BSW five, giving Rausch the majority he needed to win the post, as the other parties combined — all of which reject working with the AfD — also hold 39 seats.
The result means that member of parties besides the AfD and BSW voted for him.

Rausch, 35, thus becomes the first member of the AfD — a party classified by domestic intelligence in Saxony-Anhalt as a "confirmed right-wing extremist" organization — to become speaker in a state parliament in Germany.
The new speaker is a real-estate entrepreneur by profession and has been a member of parliament for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt since 2016.
The parliamentary session was accompanied by several anti-AfD protests in front of the parliament building.
